title: Project Policy
description: A project's declaration of which standards apply to it and at what level. Standard 18 defines the shape; Standard 19 governs this schema; ADR 0002 fixes rule identity. Keys under `rules` and `applicability` are canonical rule IDs and nothing else — the camelCase spellings that appear in the source specification are legacy aliases, are rejected here, and normalize to canonical IDs only on migration-aware input paths.

standardVersion.description: The framework version this project is evaluated against (Standard 21). An unresolvable version is a configuration error, not a compliance failure.

project.description: Project identity, carried into validator output as `project` (Standard 31 R2).

rules.description: Level per rule. A rule absent from this map takes the framework default for the declared standardVersion; a validator reports how many rules were undeclared so absence is never mistaken for a decision.

applicability.description: Whether a rule's subject exists in this project at all. First-class, and deliberately NOT an exception: `not-applicable` means the rule has no subject here, whereas an exception means the rule applies and the project is knowingly not satisfying it (Standard 34 R3, Standard 38 R3). The two must never collapse into one mechanism.

exceptions.description: Approved, time-bounded waivers of rules that DO apply (Standard 20). An expired exception is a compliance failure, not a resolution.

boundaries.description: Optional. The repository's explicit architectural boundary declaration (Standard 51 R2, ADR 0018). Absent means nothing is declared and no verdict, score or exit code changes. Present, it names the boundary members, the path each owns, the permitted dependency directions and interfaces, and the observation limits of the check that enforces it. Shape is validated here; overlap, unknown members and cyclic edges are checked by scripts/boundaries.mjs; ownership of every in-scope file and the import directions are checked against the tree by `node scripts/boundaries-check.mjs`.

attestations.description: Recorded human judgement for rules the catalog says a human evaluates (ADR 0005, added in 1.1.0). An attestation is EVIDENCE, not a waiver: it says the rule applies and is satisfied on human review. It never overrides an automated failure, never applies to a rule the catalog marks non-attestable, and returns the rule to not-evaluated once stale or expired.

boundaryPath.description: A repository-relative path using forward slashes: a file, or a directory ending in `/`. No `..`, no leading `/`, no backslash, no drive letter, no glob.

boundaryEvidence.description: `path:line` citing where the repository states or exhibits the boundary or edge.

boundaryObservation.description: The observation limits of the check, stated by the declaration itself. A claim about this repository's boundaries holds only within these limits.

method.description: How edges are observed. Only static import graphs are defined.

cannotObserve.description: Mechanisms the method cannot see. Unobserved dynamic import, reflection, generated code, subprocesses, network and data-access paths are excluded from any claim unless a detector named here covers them.

knownSites.description: Files known to use the mechanism. When the mechanism is `subprocess` the checker requires this to equal the set of in-scope files importing node:child_process, so a new site must be declared. That detects the import, never what is executed.

processExit.description: `permitted` lets files of this member call process.exit or set process.exitCode. Absent means they may not. A string rather than a boolean because the policy parser reads scalars as strings and refuses to guess types.

boundaryEdge.description: A permitted direction: files of `from` may import from files of `to`, and only the named exports in `via`. Imports within one member are always permitted. Anything else crossing members is a boundary bypass.

via.description: The permitted interface: export names, or ["*"] to permit any, stated explicitly rather than by omission.

boundaryExternal.description: Specifiers that leave the repository. A bare specifier whose prefix is not listed is an undeclared external dependency.

ruleId.description: Canonical rule identity per Standard 26 R1 and ADR 0002: `category.kebab-case-name`, dot-separated, lower-case throughout. The pattern rejects legacy camelCase aliases such as `ai.uiCapabilitiesMustBeAgentOperable` by construction.

level.description: Standard 18 R3. Levels are preferred over booleans because `true` cannot express a considered partial adoption.

note.description: Why this project selected this level. Not a substitute for an exception.

reason.description: Required. A not-applicable declaration with no reason is indistinguishable from a rule that was forgotten, which is the failure Standard 34 R3 abolishes.

reviewedAt.description: When this judgement was last examined. Not-applicable is a claim about the PROJECT, not about the rule, and stops being true the moment the project gains the capability.

revisitWhen.description: The condition under which this declaration must be re-examined — the applicability analogue of a deferred decision's trigger (Standard 41 R3).

attestationRecord.description: Either an append-only sequence of review events (the current shape) or a single record (the pre-migration shape, accepted for the migration window only). A review is an event, not mutable state: re-review appends provenance and never rewrites it, so the record proving a migration was necessary survives the migration. Supporting both shapes indefinitely is how a migration format becomes permanent architecture, so the single-record form is a ramp with an end.

attestationHistory.description: The review events for one rule, oldest first. There is deliberately no current/history split: moving a record between them would itself be a mutation, and would invite two schemas for one kind of thing. `current` is derived — the newest structurally valid event — never stored.

reviewEvent.description: One immutable review. Once written, its disposition, reviewer, timestamp, evidence, reviewed paths, and digest are history: editing any of them rewrites what a human decided at a point in time. A later judgement is recorded by appending a new event.

id.description: Stable identifier for this review event. Identity is explicit rather than positional, so reordering the file cannot silently change which review establishes the rule.

supersedes.description: The id of the review this one succeeds. It means 'this is the successor record', never 'the previous judgement was false' — a rejected historical review remains a rejected historical review forever.

status.description: Only `approved` establishes the requirement. `rejected` records that a human looked and found it unmet, which is a failure rather than silence.

evidence.description: What was examined. Required, because an attestation without it is an assertion rather than evidence — the thing this mechanism exists to avoid.

reviewedAgainst.description: What the reviewer actually looked at. The validator identifies these paths in the repository and compares; when the identity differs the attestation is stale and the rule returns to not-evaluated, because the thing reviewed is not the thing that is there now. Freshness is a separate axis from what the human decided: an approval that cannot be established as current does not establish the rule, and the reason it could not be established is reported rather than collapsed into 'nobody looked'.

digest.description: Digest of the reviewed paths. Omit it on a first pass — the validator reports the current digest so it can be recorded.

digestAlgorithm.description: How the digest was produced, named by its semantics rather than a version number. 'git-blob-set-sha256-v1' digests each reviewed path together with its committed blob identity, which is invariant across checkouts and platforms. Absence of this field means 'working-tree-bytes-sha256-v1', the superseded mechanism that hashed whatever bytes one checkout happened to materialise; such a record is classified legacy-unverifiable rather than compared, because it cannot be reproduced. A digest is never rewritten to change its algorithm — recomputing an old record under the new mechanism would upgrade the evidentiary strength of provenance without a new review.

source.description: Where content identity comes from. 'git' requires an available repository and a committed identity for every reviewed path; when either is missing the result is evidence unavailability, never staleness and never a quietly weaker substitute. Absent means git, the only source defined today.

revision.description: Informational revision identifier. Recorded, never computed — provider-neutral by design.

approvedBy.description: Provenance. An exception nobody approved is a note (Standard 20).

expires.description: Optional. Absence means the waiver is indefinite, which is a stronger claim than it looks and should be rare. An exception past its expiry is a compliance failure.

reference.description: An ADR, issue, or work item carrying the decision.
